product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: Let me say up front that my hearing is not the best at 68 but I can discern clean clear sharp audio from muffled audio and love the sound! This review is more about the general design of the HBS-730.I have been a fan of Bluetooth technology ever since Ericsson (a former employer) started putting it into their phones (pre Sony-Ericsson). I love the wireless convenience but was never quite ecstatic about its implementation until now! LG has obviously thought through the design of this device carefully and has applied good engineering where it counts--functionality--and good design where it counts--comfort and convenience.At the gym, this is the first BT hearing device that is NEVER in the way, remains in place so the buds don't fall out, provides easy to access controls that work, receives and processes interruptions to my music or audio book listening (interruptions like incoming phone calls and self-imposed outgoing phone calls) without a problem, and this device so easily deals with issues of pairing.Not only that but this device provides audible queues informing the wearer (with at least one ear bud inserted in the ear) the state of the device power switch, the state of the device battery, and the state of the device pairing.This headset is hands-down the best BT headphone device I have used, and I have invested hundreds into these things over the years since the introduction of Bluetooth in phones and headphones. One more plus... the magnetic docking of the buds into the wrap-around neck piece is ingenious and the buds almost always stay secured to their base when secured in this way. I gladly give this Bluetooth headphone my best rating.

product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: I love the freedom of wire-free ear buds. Short of buying the full headphones, and after owning a few cheap pairs of bluetooth ear buds, I finally bought this and I couldn't be happier! At first I was weary of having to "wear" the band around my neck, but that is a small compromise for the sound quality and comfort these give! I am not an audio expert, but I do like my music to sound crisp, clear, and strong in bass, and I have spent money on Bose, Senheiser, Skullcandy, Plantronics...in pursuit of the ideal.Battery life: with average of 3 hours use per day, 5 days a week, They last 4-5 days before needing to be charged again.Pairing: Easy! Turn on headset, your device detects, press "connect". Pairs in 5 seconds.Comfort: Very comfortable, although they bounce up and down on my collarbone when I run, but no big deal. The silicone tips on these are the only ones that stay in my ear, without having to switch them out for the Comply Foam ones. You do have to really push them in in order to get a good seal.Construction: The wire around the neck does seem flimsy, but I am being careful with them and give them a good wipe after sweating, because I want them to last.

product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: I paired the LG Tone with my prepaid LG Optimus Showtime cell phone and a Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 tablet. The pairings were flawless. I had no issues. The battery life is excellent. It was over 2 weeks before I charged it and it still registered "medium" which still had battery life. I highly recommend this bluetooth. product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: I had the HBS-730 in black and loved it, unfortunately it fell off me when I was thrown in an accident and since I was in full adrenaline panic mode at the time I didn't notice they were not on me until I got home.So I bought this in white only because the white was $10 cheaper, I don't care $10 worth about the color though I prefer black if all things are equal.Now I wish I'd gone with the black but I wore these for a week before I realized it and had thrown out the packaging already. I'll keep them, I'll use them, and I'd probably even love them if I hadn't had the the other set before, here is why:- This is stupid perhaps but this headset uses a different voice than my last one, sounds like just some random lady at the office that they recorded, I don't like her voice where before I'd really not noticed.- When the headset is low on batteries it gives you a warning, waits a while and then warns you again. My old one did this too but infrequently enough that I could keep listening to my music for a while. Important sometimes for that last 2 stops on the train or the last 5 minutes of my run! Give me the warning well ahead of time so I know to charge it but give me time to actually listen. This new one? Once the voice says the battery is low there is no point to continuing to listen because she interrupts the music/phone every 5 seconds to tell me the battery is low. I wonder how much battery time is wasted with that but it is so annoying that I just turn the damn thing off.- The bluetooth signal is just a bit weaker. Sometimes I lose signal when my phone is in my purse as my purse swings around behind me, one of the things I loved about the 730 before was that it was the first stereo headset I'd found that reliably maintained the signal through my body (I'm a totally average sized woman), this is still better than the others I'd tried just not perfect.I don't know if this is a difference between white and black versions/batches or if the quality in this model went downhill or what but there is definitely a difference. I suppose compared against other stereo headsets I'd tried I'd still give it 5 stars but compared against the other of the same model: 4 stars
summary: Not as good as the black version ... the only difference should be color, but it isn't

product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: I'm entirely unimpressed by this device. I don't know, maybe it's me.First off, this seems like it might be a knock off device, not the one pictured. As someone else mentioned, the on/off switch is reversed, there are silver bands on the earbuds which aren't on the promo images. But maybe there are slight variations based on the assembly from different plants. The other reviewer also mentioned there was no LG logo on his device. I didn't see one either, but there was a small sticker where the logo should have been with the words "TEAR INVALID" on it. Underneath that sticker was the LG logo. Very odd. Seems almost like a non-english speaker attempting to prevent me from removing the sticker, that it may invalidate the warranty? Just guessing here.At first I had tremendous trouble pairing the device with my Samsung Galaxy S3. The instructions (which don't appear all that professional) say to turn the power on, and the blue LED will light solid. Of course they don't tell you where the blue LED is. I can't find one anywhere. The only thing that lights up is the red ring around the "call" button when I plug in the charger cord. So I tried the manual pairing method. That seemed to work (though no blue light appeared anywhere), I got it to play some music. But the sound was pretty bad. Muffled, not much treble, as compared to my wired earbuds I got with my Galaxy. But when I turned the power off, and back on, it didn't reconnect with my phone. Even the manual pairing method wouldn't work after that.So I figured maybe the battery was low, there doesn't seem to be any way to tell. I let it charge for about 15 mins, then powered it on. The red ring around the call button began to flicker and the headset vibrated a couple times, and it connected to my phone. I got it to play some more music again, but the sound was no better.So my plan is to give it a good charge overnight, and see if it acts any better. Though if the sound remains as bad as it is, I'll be sending it back, and requesting a non-knock-off version.

product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: I have owned a number of Bluetooth headphones over the years, but none for about 5 years due to: (a) the fact that I always ended up losing them, and (b) the audio (sent and received) was always relatively poor.On a whim, I purchased these (HBS-730), and I love them. I realize that others have said the range is bad, but my phone is apparently always close enough to me that it isn't an issue. I've had no dropped audio whatsoever.For the price - under $50 - you can't go wrong as long as you're OK with the basic premise of the design. These wrap around your neck (or, for me, go under the collar of my shirt). For some, that might be uncomfortable. I don't notice that I'm wearing them.I love the fact that I can wear either of the earpieces (or both of them, of course) without affecting the microphone, which is located on the left end of the main body. Since one of my uses for these is talking while driving, and since I can't legally drive with both ears plugged, the design allows me to use either ear (and to switch ears) without the listener being affected. Audio is easily loud enough for calls with one earpiece in, and especially good with them both in (when at home, for example).I also am quite happy that these use a micro USB port for charging (as do most of my devices) and also came with a charger (which is worth something in and of itself). No extra proprietary cords when traveling are needed, and I've got another charger I can use with any USB charging cable (I don't think it's extraordinarily powerful, but it'll slowly charge just about anything).The audio when listening to music is stellar. Not audiophile-grade, mind you, but *vastly* better than I was expecting from something in this price range that included the Bluetooth circuitry, a charger, a cable, and so on. Most plain headphones at this price don't sound as good, and few sound much better.Finally, one of the potential drawbacks - the size - is, to me, a benefit. I'm far less likely to lose these.Are there nits to pick? Sure, but nothing significant, and none that take away from my rating for these in their price range.

product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: I just bought these headphones for a business trip to a major city, and my impression is: Wow. The LG Tone+ is everything I want in a set of in-ear headphones. Note that these were tested on a Samsung Galaxy S5, which naturally has enormous Bluetooth range- I can leave my phone in a room and be across the parking lot before the connection drops.Pros:-AptX. If your phone supports the AptX protocol, you will hear CD-quality sound. (Note that despite not saying so on the website, the S5 does support AptX).-Yes, that means good sound! I'm an audiophile with extra-sensitive hearing, and these headphones are as good as you can possibly get in this price range. I listen to dance music (driving bass), rock music (midrange), and audiobooks (voice, treble). All sound as good as I can get with a full set of speakers.-Cool design. Of course the neckband is mostly to store the batteries and antennas necessary to make the Bluetooth work, but having extra controls and magnetic rests for the earbuds makes them very cool.-Good signal. After a good 8 hours of use, I've had a handful of brief stutters that resolved automatically within a fraction of a second. My phone has been in a front pocket, a jacket, a backpack, across the room- it's great.-Good battery. I had a 4-hour train ride and I think the batteries were only down to what the announcer said was "power medium". Very nice.-Good sound dampening. Even when not in use, I sometimes used the earbuds to block our sound- like when passing a train engine at a train station. The earbuds can completely dampen the normal hum of a city, including nature sounds and distant vehicles. That's more than enough for me.-Easy "one-ear" use. If I need to listen- say, as I'm crossing traffic- I can pop out one earbud and use the magnet to hold it to the neck piece. Once I'm done, pop it back into my ear. Simple, easy, effective.Cons:-The magnets holding the earbuds are kind of weak, so they pop out easily in a pocket or just as you move. I leave it on my neck as much as possible.-Wire management can be an issue. It's not as bad as a traditional wire, but the design could use some minor tweaks. For example, why don't the wires just travel inside the loop for most of their distance? This would be an easy way to pin them back out of the way for most people.-App support for buttons is not perfect. My favorite apps (Play Music, DI.fm) only "sort of" recognize the fast-forward or play-pause buttons. I can usually stop music (hold the play/pause button), and track skip will work but I can't fast-forward within a track. Considering that these are fairly popular apps I'm wondering if I should look into a firmware update for the headphones. Regardless, volume and power always work, so that has me covered.Overall:-Competitively priced, great audio, great connection, great batteries. What else could a person ask for in a headset? I wish there was a version of this same product with over-the-ear headphones, but this is as good as you can ask for in-ear headphones.

product_name: Spigen Ultra Thin Slim Armor Case
text: 07/14/2014 *** Update***I've had this set for over a year now. What was good is still good, when the connectivity is there. When riding my motorcycle and the phone is mounted on my handlebars with nothing between me and the phone, connectivity is good and stays there.When I am doing yard work and the phone is on my right hip, connectivity is iffy. And I get complaints of echoing and such intermittently. I thought is was my phone because I had the Android 4.3 upgrade which trashed my wi-fi and I thought might have impacted my bluetooth as well but two weeks ago, I finally got a replacement phone. The new Phone (Galaxy Note 2-Verizon) accepted the 4.3 and 4.4.2 updates with no issue to my wi-fi this time(YEA!) but the bluetooth issues are still there. My son has the same headset with a galaxy S4 and the same problems. My wife has the same headset on her Iphone-4 and no issues. Go figure.So, my recommendation is this:1) Buy it, try it out heavily and return it if it does not work.2) If you have problems, Do not wait to return it or maybe get a fix from LG. I waited too long and the warranty ran out.When it works, the sound is GREAT. Good bass (well, let's just say my ears like it but I do have a bit of hearing loss so fidelity is no big deal for me). Good volume. Works great with my laptop and android tablet.The sad part is a cheap Bluetooth v2.1 works better with my phone than this one.I purchased this headset for one specific reason. To be able to listen to music and communicate on the phone when riding my motorcycle. I did not purchase through Amazon but a local big box store who did price match Amazon.I am going to look for a Bluetooth v4.0. maybe that will work better. Note, the v2.1 that work better fit me terribly. I've got a big head and those did not have enough STRETCH to get around the back of my head.Setup Description:I have the LG730 paired with a Galaxy Note II phone (Verizon). The phone does not have the stock battery, it has a 9300mah extended battery(warranty ZeroLemon Protection Guarantee CompatibleI mention this because it may be part of the problem I do occasionally have with the headset under the CON section. I use the case provided by ZeroLemon for my phone.I mount my Galaxy Note 2 on my motorcycle (2007 Goldwing) using a RAM Mount for the phone (RAM Universal X Grip Tablet Tabletsand the handlebar (RAM Mounting RAM B 174 LO4U Reservoir Lowrance. I bought the wrong phone mount initially but just flipped the prongs around to the smaller set on the back and it works great. No fear of vibration. I used it on a 1600 mile trip two weeks ago with no problems.I have a 3/4 Vega helmet with a face shield that I usually have lowered. I also wear a heavy motorcycle jacket (not a leather jacket but a heavy duty nylon jacket with Kevlar protectors and such). The LG730 sits inside the jacket and I zip the jack all the way up but leave the collar open to be able to get to the answer button. The ear buds have no issues as long as I have them stretched out all the way. I only wear one, not two when riding so check your state laws on that ([...] I can turn my head left or right and not pull the bud out of my right ear.Usage Experience:PRO:Sound Quality: Excellent compared to the helmet speakers I was using. Good Bass and volume levels that are adjustable both on the phone and the headset so you can get the mix you want. I am NOT an audiophile so I'm not concerned about the highest hi's or the lowest lows. I just want to hear the music and hold a conversation.Microphone: Very Good. I made several test calls to multiple people while riding my motorcycle. Up until about 40 MPH, they could not tell I was on a motorcycle. Up to about 70MPH, all they heard was a bit of a buzz from my mufflers but could still hear me clearly and I could hear them quite well.Call notification: Works well. I can hear the phone ringing in my ear bud, the phone itself and vibration from the HB730.Call Answer: Works well with bare fingers and light gloves. Harder to get with thick gloves but doable (Auto answer would be nice).Wearing: They are very flexible and comfortable to wear.CONS:When not on the motorcycle, I wear my phone on my right hip. Sometimes the sound quality goes to pot listening to music while walking. I"ll get skips in my songs. This never happens on the same songs with my wired headset. Turning off and back on the Tone+ usually clears that issue. it's not an issue with the battery life (Usually high or on medium) and my phone with the 9300mah battery is NEVER low. :) (Love that battery....)I've noticed that when I lift up my left arm, i lose significant signal. I've got a normal arm, no metals or anything in it but the blue tooth connections severely weakens and the sound almost drops out completely. Drop my left arm back down, I'm good to go. (This may be related to my extended battery which completely covers the back of my Note 2 phone. I'll find my original battery and see if I can duplicate the problem.No auto-answer. Would be nice when working out or riding so I don't have to take a hand off of my handle bar.Hard to find the manual on the LG website. An odd CON but I was just looking for it(to see if it can auto answer) and finding any support document for the LG Tone+ other than the sales page just wasn't there.Summary.Even with the small cons listed, this is a great Bluetooth headset for my purposes. I also exercise at the gym with them. I don't run (yet) but do walk on the treadmill and no problems to date with the slipping off. Running might cause a problem because the are not tight around the back of my neck and may bounce.If it ever breaks, I'll buy it again.
summary: An imperfect setup with a Samsung Galaxy Note 2(Verizon).

text: I've had my set for about two weeks now. My goal was a headset for running and training for a tough mudder as well as for my motorcycle.Sound quality is great. The bass is slightly lacking but overall pretty good for an earbud set. Noise isolating helps drown outside sound, but is not noise canceling. When used as a headset on the phone, the buttons and features work great. Haven't had anyone complain while talking to them.Battery life seems pretty good. Two weeks of training about an hour or two a day and it still says high battery.Range is one thing I have seen comments on a lot. I have no problems. I leave my phone on the treadmill and walk over to a pull up rack about 20' away with absolutely no issues. I don't know why you would wander any further than that away.Gaming is one place I see a slight issue. To get the quality across Bluetooth they must compress the data because there is a slight delay on fast paced games. I tried a few online and hard drive videos, and the lag wasn't as noticeable.Running with these has one slight issue as well. The front portions of the neck piece that contain the controls tend to bounce onto my collarbone. This got annoying, and I'm sure it isn't that good for the headset to bounce off bone nonstop. I remedied this by putting the end pieces under my shirt collar. This prevented the bounce, but they do get awfully sweaty now. Only time will tell how they hold up to the sweat.I am eagerly awaiting motorcycle season in Wisconsin to test them out on the road.Overall I am very happy with the purchase and have recommended it to others.

text: I've had the original Tone headphones (HBS-700) on my Wish List for some time and finally received them for Christmas this year. Let me tell you something: I had NO idea what I was missing! If I'd realized how great these headsets were, I would have purchased them for myself a long time ago.In the few days I have had them, I've easily used them for several multi-hour sessions (watching movies at night on my Tablet or music on my phone) with NO discomfort. In fact, I find it difficult to find earbuds small enough to comfortably fit my ears for more than a half an hour, but the default installed earbuds fit perfectly! (There are two additional, larger sets included).On top of that, at night I put on a movie or show on Netflix to fall asleep to, but wear headphones so as to not wake my spouse. Prior to receiving these, my favorite set have been a wired set of Vizio, which, if I rolled to my side, would become uncomfortable in the ear pressed into my pillow, and are often yanked out as the wire would get tangled up as I rolled around in my sleep.These have such a low profile in the ear that there is no pressure or discomfort when laying on my side. Even more impressive is that they remain in place even after moving around in my sleep. I just remove them on my first arousal after falling asleep. Even after using them the night before, I can use them the following day for several hours before recharging them for the next night.Ultimately, after only a few days, I purchased this model, the Tone+ (HBS-730), but kept the HBS-700 model for my spouse. The Tone+ solves my only gripe with the standard model: the lack of a mute; a necessary feature for professional conference calls. The Tone+ also add several improvements including a vibration alert for incoming calls and best of all, the ability for the Tone+ to be actively paired with 2 devices simultaneously (be it 2 phones or a phone and a tablet, for example).I am simply stunned by the quality and features available for the Tone+ given the price. It's hard to find a quality set of wired headsets, or a single-ear headset for this price.In short, I am very impressed and am very happy with this product that I use daily.PROs:+Extremely comfortable.+Very good sound quality for the average user.+Impressive battery life.+Simultaneous active pairing to 2 devices+OUTSTANDING VALUE (hard to beat the price/quality even compared to a quality wired headset)NEUTRAL:=Noise-blocking earbuds. Great for focusing on a conversation or your media. However, less useful for use with a Playstation and dangerous if used while driving (I have a standard headset for these situations).=The thin wire connecting the earbuds to the base may not be as durable long-term as some heavier-duty wired earbuds. However, there is almost never any tension on the earbud wires. But, given that I use them to sleep, I've purchased a 3-year replacement plan through Squaretrade for $10 (30% off) that even covers wear and tear.=SMS Text Reader app was not personally tested, but Android Play Store reviews seem to indicate that the required app is hit or miss based on your specific device.CONs:-Sound quality may not stack up for a true audiophile.-The Bluetooth connection can be tempermental. Even the human body, if place between the device and the headset (such as putting your phone in a back pocket) has the potential to interfere with the signal. This is personally a rare problem, but a surprising one when it occurs.

text: Pros:The microphone quality on the Tone+ HBS-730 is much much better when compared to the previous model. The stereo audio quality is also noticeably better. The additional features are well worth the price of the upgrade. I personally appreciate the ability to connect to two Bluetooth devices at once allowing me to use both my laptop and cellphone in cafes and airport lounges. Carefully following the written directions I paired the Tone+ first with my MBP then manually paired it with my Android cellphone, this sequence makes the cell my primary device and my laptop my secondary. When a call comes in I can press the MBP mute button and the cellphone takes over the audio on the device.Cons:The Tone+ has a severely limited range when compared to its predecessor. When wearing winter clothing, if I put the phone in my rear jeans pocket the cell phone will disconnect from the Tone+. While placing the device in my front right jeans pocket, if I turn my body to the left and look up (placing my body between the left call button on the Tone+ and the cell phone's "chin" region) I will disconnect the cellphone and the Tone+. With the device in my front-right pocket, if my wife gives me a hug, I will disconnect the device. I suspect larger people might have more of a problem as I can get the device to disconnect by wrapping my hand around the right part of my cellphone. That indicates the signal doesn't do well with transmitting through the body... and the meatier you are... the more problems you may have. To work around this disconnect problem I keep the device in a breast pocket while using the head phones in winter clothing... in thinner clothing this disconnecting behavior is harder to reproduce for me.Use the Tone+ with a chest or arm pocket and don't let it stray too far from its connected devices. When you move out of range and drop connection some devices (My MBP for example) will require you to turn off the Tone+ and turn it back on. The previous model could handle a good 30 feet while this model seems to be limited to 10 feet.In spite of these problems, I still rate the device very high because it is the only device I've found on the market that will let me switch between two bluetooth devices, has good stereo sound, a good microphone, and very nice voice prompts. This version also features a very very useful *mute* feature you toggle on and off by holding down the volume up and down buttons simultaneously for a second. This and the form factor are worth any other hassles. Just make sure you have a chest or arm pocket to carry it in when wearing a heavy jacket. The bluetooth antenna on this device seems to be on the left so a left side arm pocket is probably the best place for your cellphone.*tl;dr* for the price this device is fantastic (it is even better than some devices twice its price) but it has very poor range and won't work if you place enough of your body between the bluetooth transmitter and it.EDIT: Using the Tone+ with my cellphone is rather straight forward but, after some use I've figured out this process to get the MacBook Pro to use the audio headset at the same time as the cell phone: First complete the dual pairing procedure as documented in the LG Tone+ handbook starting with the MBP then the cell phone. Next: to start any dual use session 1) turn off bluetooth on all devices 2) turn on bluetooth on the MacBook Pro, 3) Turn on the LG Tone+ and select it as the audio out on the MacBook 4) turn on the Cell Phone's bluetooth and manually select the LG Tone+ You have to repeat steps 1 to 4 every time you start up any device, reboot, or walk out of range.
summary: Tone+ is a good upgrade to the Tone, with some minor problems.

The item also works very good with theNew Trent Powerpak 10.0 10000mAh Pocket Friendly Portable Dual USB Port External Battery Charger/Power Pack for Smartphones and Tablets and morewhich I got along with the charger, it charges the backup battery at a good rate and doesn't take too long. So far, this charger has worked with every item that I have tried and have had no compatibility problems with it at all. I would have to say that this charger charges my devices at a rate which is somewhat faster than the chargers that were supplied with the phone. Although I do not have recorded statistics, it seems that it did charge my devices faster. I also like how the prongs are foldable which save space. When compared to an iPad charger, the size is similar except this provides two charging ports whereas the ipad charger only comes with one. I do feel that the charger is a bit big, but I guess that has to be the size in order to include two ports. The charger has a solid feel and hopefully has solid build quality.This is the perfect tool for me as I always only have enough plugs to charge one device at a time, but now with this device with two ports, I can charge my iPad and iPhone at the same time thus having access to both of them the next day as currently I only charge my phone and not my iPad so one has lower battery. The only thing I wish is that it showed which port corresponded to what charging mode it is on, I believe that there is a slower/regular charging mode and a fast mode for bigger items. I also noticed that the back of the is shiny whereas the body is matte, it would have been nice if all of it was matte. Finally I found that it does take up quite alot of room on the wall plug and when plugged into my surge protector, it can take up two slots depending on the plug.I do know that chargers get hot when charging, but I found that this one does indeed get quite hot when in use especially when charging multiple items. I will be on the lookout to make sure the temperature of the thing isn't too crazy. The price is good, except I feel that if it were cheaper a few dollars, it would be a best hit right away. Unfortunately it seems that my unit did not come with any instructions so I was quite puzzled of which usb port did what but this is the plug that I will use on trips and more.I will add more as I use this charger, hopefully it will last!

This little but sturdy device worked terrific. I used this product during Hurricane Sandy when I travelled to work or other locations to charge my mobile devices and mobile power banks for when I was home without power. This product really came in handy. It was small enough to fit in my pocket for travel without being overly bulky or having prongs sticking into me and it easily unfolded and was able to very quickly power any two devices I plugged into it very quickly and without any issues. I charged cableless power banks like the New Trent NT70T and IMP52D as well as Android smart phones and ipod touches and even power hungry tablets like my Ipad and Nexus 7 tablets with ease. I even used it to power as well as charge a Sony High Speed Video camera simply and without issue. It had the power to handle two tablets or any combination of other devices without having a problem and charged them very quickly and was recognized by all products whether apple or android as well as other devices without issue. It was a life saver to be able to charge multiple devices using only one outelt in a short period of time at locations I wasn't at very long so I could have powered devices during my extended power outage. This was a really great device that worked flawlessly and made a very tough situation much easier.

First impressions:Mechanically, the charger seems overall well built. The case of the chargeris a quality textured plastic (good for not showing scratches andfingerprints). The collapsable plug blades are convenient, and are verysturdy. They latch both in and out with enough detent that I'm not fightingwith it collapsing while I'm trying to insert it into the wall. The chargeras a whole isn't the smallest charger I own, but that's not really an issuefor me. This is the kind of charger I will leave plugged into a power stripand never take anywhere. Also, there is a dim blue power LED visiblethrough a "window" on one side of the charger. I'm glad it's not way toobright, as most consumer electronics LEDs are, but this one is almost toodim. I was surprised it had a light at all, though, and it is usefulfeedback about whether the device has power or not without keeping youawake at night.The only minor criticism I have for the body of the charger is the shinyplastic face on the side where the USB ports are. It gives the device aslightly cheaper look. It's a purely cosmetic issue, and certainly not onethat would make or break the purchase for me.Before I go into performance of the charger, I will share that I havelearned a valuable lesson: cables DO matter! I will admit, when I firsttried to charge my LG G2 with the NT-90C, I was less than impressed. I useda thin, short cable I had gotten for free with an external battery pack,and the phone complained that the charger was not compatible with thephone. The iPad/Smartphone port would slow charge the phone, but I couldnot get the other port to work at all. I was ready to write the charger offas a poor product.Later, I gathered up several of my chargers and evaluated all of them withmy G2 for how many mA of current each would supply to my phone (using theBattery Monitor Widget app on the Play Store). To my surprise, several ofmy known-good chargers were failing to correctly charge the phone! Forsanity's sake, I switched out the cable to the one that came with the G2,and lo and behold, all was well again. So to anyone who is having troublewith this or any other charger- make sure the CABLE is capable of handlingthe charging current! I think the G2 is a particularly picky phone (itseems to only fast charge with it's own pack-in cable and no other), but Iimagine this could be the case for many phones. Don't throw out a goodcharger just because you have a weak cable!Performance:Now that I had the correct cable, time to evaluate some wall chargers andsee how the New Trent NT-90C stacks up:First, I measured the current each charger was outputting to my phone. Thisis measured using a Verizon Wireless LG G2 phone running the BatteryMonitor Widget app. Each result was averaged over a few minutes to makesure the reading was accurate.New Trent NT-90C "Tablet/Smartphone" port rated: 2.1A to G2:1,367mANew Trent NT-90C "iPad/Smartphone" port rated: 2.1A to G2:1,516mALG MCS-04WR (packed with G2) rated: 1.8A to G2:1,456mASamsung ETA0U61JBE (packed with Galaxy S3) rated: 1.0A to G2:662mASamsung ETA0U80JBE (packed with Galaxy Nexus) rated: 1.0A to G2:631mANo-Name (packed with pocket router) rated: 1.0A to G2:641mAI wish I had a tablet to test the full 2.1A output of the charger. Withjust a smartphone, though, this is as fast of a charger as you will find.Smartphones will only charge up to a certain rate, which appears to be 1.5Awith the G2, and the NT-90C handles that just fine. It performed evenbetter than the OEM LG charger at charging my G2. I also charged a SamsungGalaxy S3, which charged at least as fast as it's included charger as well.Overall I give the NT-90C a 5 out of 5. It does exactly what it is supposedto do: quickly charge my phone. It is well built, and besides a few minorcosmetic quibbles, looks pretty darn good!

I used the the USB Wall charger with an iPhone 5 and 5s and also an iPad Air and iPad mini.The iPad/Smartphone USB slot definitely charges iPads quickly. My tests showed about 1-2 mins for 1%.The Tablet/Smartphone USB slot felt a little slow in charging my iPhones though. In 30 mins, my phone started at 60% and ended at 76%. But this seems to be pretty standard even with the Apple OEM charger.I like the dual feature of this wall charger and that the prongs can be folded in for safe portability. Great for trips or even at home. Can have an iPhone and iPad/Tablet charging while taking up half an outlet.

If your looking to save some space, this charger does the job. It handles two different devices just fine. The folding plugs are my favorite feature, it makes it nice for traveling or storing. In my house my Husband and I are always fighting over the one electrical outlet by the bed, usually I have to wait until morning to charge my phone, now we can both be happy.

I was surprised the two ports were not equal, when charging my ipad mini. But it wasn't a big deal. However, this is a big upgrade from the 10w charger that came with the device. It takes about half the time to charge my ipad mini with this product as opposed to using the factory apple one. The dual usb design saves space when charging my tablet and phone at the same time which is very convenient. And the product is very built well and has a sturdy feel. Very satisfied with this wall charger.For mine, there is a small blue led light that turns on when it is plugged in. It's not too bright but it lets you know whether or not the charger is getting electricity run through it.

Product was packaged extremely well, did not have any issues with damage. Only the terminal is included, does not include the usb cable (bummer, can never have too many usb cables)My first impression of the product when i opened is was that the wall charger had an sleek design with power terminals that retract back into the body of the charger for extra space saving and efficiency. Its a big bonus for people who travel a lot or want to use this as a spare charger. The charger also has dual usb outlets which was extremely useful to me as i use it in the family room, where everyone in my family fights for juice for their electronics, and as far as i could tell both the usb outlets receive the same amount of power; however i did notice when 2 tablets are charging it does take a little longer than some of the other chargers i have used. Compared to my OEM samsung charger, i did not notice any difference in the amount of time it took to charge my Galaxy s3. Approximately took 3.5 hours to recharge fully from 4% on my galaxy s3 (phone was on regular mode with light usage)Both the usb outlets are on the face of the charger, although i did not mind this, i could see how this could be an issue for someone who would want to put it behind a bed/nightstand as it would put unnecessary strain and damage to the usb wire (had similar problems with previous oem HTC chargers)There is also a blue led light to indicate it is receiving power. Seems solely aesthetic.The overall build quality is excellent, i just wish the dual usb outlets could be relocated to each SIDE of the unit, instead of on the face of it.If you are in need of a charger to place in your family room or for travel, i would highly recommend this device.

This is my review of the New Trent 10W 5V/2A high-speed Dual Port USB AC wall charger. I ordered the dual port wall charger to be able to simultaneously charge my iPhone 5 and iPad mini. This adapter helps me to achieve this by providing the proper amps for my devices and fully charging both devices quickly. Unfortunately, the charger's ports are not labeled, so you have to figure out which port works best for your specific device. On my charger when plugged into the wall socket, the led indicator light and the wording on the face of the charger are at the top of the device. The top port works fine for charging my iPhone 5 and the bottom port for my iPad mini. If I attempt to charged my iPad in the wrong port, I get the "not charging" icon for my iPad's battery status. It would have been a bit more user friendly if the ports had something to differentiate the two, but this is not considered a deal breaker for purchasing the product in my opinion.This space-saving adapter is compact and lightweight, made of durable high quality plastic and has folding electrical prongs, all of which make it ideal for easy transport and travel. My overall rating of the New Trent Dual Port high-speed USB AC wall adapter is 4.5/5 stars with a 1/2 star deduction for the little difficulty it takes the consumer to figure out which port can be used for a specific device. If New Trent were to fix this oversight in their next update of the product, I would certainly give it 5 stars, and I definitely recommend purchasing this USB AC adapter if you have more than one next-generation electronic device.

This charger does what is says, charges two devices at once. I like it because of it's 2.1A charge rate and nice design. The foldable plug is also a small plus.My only issue is I would like the unit to be smaller. It takes up a large portion of my sockets and makes little room for other plugs.I currently use it next to my computer to charge my phone and wireless mouse at the same time.

NT90CWhat can I possible say about a usb wall charger? I bought 2 of them because I lost my iphone 4 wall charger, and was left with only my iphone 5 wall charger. I was afraid of being without any at all, so I figure having a few extra is not a bad idea.The price was extremely reasonable and I really like the fact that the charger has 2 usb outlets. When you have a household with as many devices as ours, you start running out of plugs very quickly to charge things. So, what seems like a minor thing, really ends up being a big convenience.I occasionally charge my ipad along with my iphone, (works perfect), But I mainly use this to charge my New Trent battery chargers 2 at a time and that also works great! All works well and everything seems to charge pretty quick.I also like the fact that the prongs fold into the charger to make it even smaller and easier to store.Definitely recommend.
Nice to eliminate one more charger plugged into the wall. Compact, easy to use. Nice that you can plug in two USB devices at once.

Construction is solid with visible indicators for specs and slot type. Product outputs at specified amperage as long as a good USB cable is used.It would have been nice to see the slot type on all sides though.

Compact and immensely useful, this little charger block is handy to have around the house, or when traveling. It charges 2 devices simultaneously, a big improvement over every other charger I have yet it retains the same form factor. It's almost the same size as the iPad power block. The prongs fold down for easier storage and portability.I've used it with my iPad 3, iPhone 4S, and Kindle Keyboard so far. A sturdy and versatile travel companion or home charger and value-priced also and solidly constructed. Highly recommended.
summary: Handy little charger that charges 2 devices at once

text: I read the reviews and saw that most people liked this charger and they said it worked well. I ordered one and it arrived today. I plug it and began to check the output. Neither port will get above 820mA, one port gets 820 and the other gets 640mA. This was a waste of my time ordering. Don't make the same mistake I did.11/9/13After leaving the first review I was contacted by company and was told they were refunding my money for this and they were shipping me a new one at no cost. After about a week the new one arrived. It still does not have the 2.1 A output but it does get a whole lot closer. I only get 1.7 and 1.1 A but that's a huge improvement so I am rating this 4 stars.

Replaced two separate usb chargers and is keeping both my Nexus 7 and Iphone 5 juiced up at the wall. This would also be the charger I'd take with me on travel where I'd need multiple USB chargers. The overall charger design is simple but it might block another outlet depending on the orientation of your powerstrip outlets or whatever else you have plugged in at the wall. The foldable plug also makes it easy to fold it up and throw in a bag for travel. Solid and simple item at a much cheaper price than buying separate chargers.

Pros: Small and compact, sleek design and packaging, frees up an outlet and charges my devices quickly.Cons: Did warm up a little while charging, but not too bad.Overall: Overall its a great little charger to have. We have a place on the counter where we charge our iPads (1 3rd Gen and 2 minis). It is nice to be able to charge two devices at once as there is only one free outlet in that area. I haven't had any issues with the charger so far. I would recommend it.

This was so easy to store and use, it fit in my clutch. I wish it was labelled, and I cannot attest to the actual speed except on the EVO which did charge in half the time it normally takes. Even if it does not actually charge faster on all devices it is ultra portable, the prongs fold in and it fits darn near anywhere. I love it.

This item works great. I use it to charge my Samsung Galaxy S 3 and my kindle. Freed up an outlet beside my nightstand. Charges my devices just as fast as their stock chargers. Would recommend and have recommended this product to others.

I was happy to get this product because we have many different products that need to be charged, 3 iPhones , 2 iPad's , and a Kindle and an iPod. OFTEN my daughter needs to charge an item at the same time as I do, and the Kindle doesn't come with a wall charger, so I have to use my brick to charge her Kindle. This item has been a life saver at charging two items at a time! I love the blue light that lets me know I am plugged in. Often I plug my phone in behind my bed, and I can just glance back and see that it is plugged in (I sometimes trip over the wire and unplug it!) The only issue I have had with this, and it may be the issue with my iPad, is once it was plugged in, and the iPad was plugged in, but it said "Not Charging" at the top. I unplugged the twice, to no avail, then I unplugged the wall adapter and plugged it back in, and it worked fine! I am very happy with this item, and have told several people about it, especially those with multiple devices!

This is my 7th New Trent item. This New Trent 10W 5V-2A Dual USB Port high-speed AC Wall Charger and it's a useful convenient item to have given all the electronics I have in my home and the limited electrical outlets. It's not bulky and the prongs can fold in for travel. It's powerful and and can be used internationally as it can take AC 100-240V. The top usb port is labeled "Tablet/Smartphone" and bottom USB port is labeled "iPad/Smartphone"...The description on Amazon says "Split between two ports, alternate between charging 2 Smartphones at 1 amp each or a tablet device at 2.1 amps." However, it does appear the ports operate differently and perhaps at different outputs(?). I have a Samsung Galaxy Tab (1st generation) and it seems to be able to charge on both USB slots -- however, it gives me a normal "green indicator" on my status bar when charging on the top USB slot but when a "green with red X" indicator when I charge it on the bottom USB slot. I am able to charge my Samsung Galaxy S4 smartphone with both slots without any issues. I like it and would recommend to my friends and family.

Traveling from airports to airports can be hectic. One of my biggest concern is whether my devices will be charged before I reach my destination. This wall charger is small enough, that you can throw it in your backpack. It can in handy the last time I was at LAX and I had to charge both my tablet and my phone. There were very few ports available, but by plugging this in one of the very few outlets available. The charges to both my phone and tablets keep me alive so I can fully charge my device at the hotel. The price for this device is fair and could always be a lifesaver for travelers.

I bought this for my samsung galaxy s4 and samsung galaxy note 10.1 2014 edition. While it is compact with a nice swivel plug, it charged my devices SLOWLY. I turned off devices over night, plugged them in, and 8 hours later they were only at ~75%. Perhaps I got a bad one, given the many positive reviews, but for me, I need devices to charge faster and this was way below expectation.
Works very well charging 2 USB items quickly. I often use it for charging cell phones, cameras and newtrent battery backups.

OK. What can you say about a wall-charger plug? It's neat because you can plug two cords into it & charge your smartphone and tablet or two peripherals at the same time on one cord. The pricing is good too and I'm always losing these gizmos and having to replace. So I highly recommend this plug. I'll always buy a dual from now on. Why not? Better to have an extra port and NOT need it, than to need TWO and not HAVE it, don't ya know!

Ever notice how long it takes to charge your iphone 5, external battery (I have a new trent) or ipad mini via usb? Ever notice all devices charge via USB and a POS A/C corder adapter? I did! A little bit of research, I found out how these devices charge from a computer, they are ONLY allowed so much power because of possible overheating, surges, etc. Dun du du da! The ultimate solution, the New Trent NT90C Wall charger. Pros: 2 USBs ports, it actually charged my iphone and ipad twice as fast as the normal methods at the same time (I'm a virgo, we analyze everything). Great portability, I take it on the go and the prongs fold down, no bends or bust. Try buying an apple replacement, and you will hand over a lot more. Cons: none. To rate, it hits the top of the mark, a 5 out of 5 with 5 being the highest. OH, and if you have a bulldog that will eat anything... my New Trent survived an entire minute. Slobber wiped right off and back to charging it went.

Have been a fan of this brand's batteries and decided to get this after my prior AC-to-USB charger broke and gave me a nasty shock. This feels better built and I appreciate the labels (that don't show up on the Amazon product page as of 11/2013): one says tablet/smartphone (presumably 1amp) and one iPad/smartphone (presumably 2.1amp). So if you have an iPhone and an iPad you might as well get one of these for work, home traveling, etc. and have one fewer thing to plug in.
summary: Does what it's supposed to; one USB outlet can charge iPad

text: Charges Samsung Note 2 and Nexus 7 quickly and without issue. Has lasted so far without incident since purchase in January 2014. Used in conjunction with Mediabridge USB 2.0 Micro-USB to USB cable.

The 5V/2A Dual USB Ports high-speed AC Wall Charger was very easy to use and charged my iPod right away. This is a great size, usable for many devices and will be great to use when traveling and at my office. I recently had an unexpected health crisis with a family member and within 1 day at the hospital my iPod and phone lost their battery charge. I was unable to get home to get my charger for 4 days. If I had this, I would have been able to charge my electronics immediately and stay in contact easier with people. It is a nice compact size and does what I need it to do. I wish I had it a couple of months ago, it would have helped immensely. I give it 5 stars. It is a great size, doesn't weigh much at all, and easy to carry around. It is very helpful to have.

The most I've measured on this charger was around 1.6A charging with only one cable plugged in. But then not even my OEM Samsung charger for my Note 2 (that was rated for 2.0A) was charging at anything more than 1.8A. Just know this going in and you won't be too disappointed (if you ignore the fact that it's RATED at 2.0A)
summary: works great but does not charge at full 2.0A

text: I have Samsung Galaxy S4 and Note 8.0. This can charge both at the same time, the 2A (upper one) is for Note, the 1A (lower, near the fine print) is for S4. There is NOTHING to complain about this charger. Solid built, and the time to charge the battery to 100% is much less than the one coming with the phone.

The New Trent Dual Port AC Charger (NT90C) has been a great product so far. I used this product to charge my New Trent powerpak xtreme 12,000 mAh battery bank and took little to no time to charge that baby all the way up. I like the dual port design so I don’t have to keep sharing my wall wart with a friend and keep switching off, both my friend and I can charge our phones at the same time with this charger. I like the sleep matte black design on the product and had a solid feel to the hand. One thing I don’t like about this product is that the top and bottom usbs are different, It would have been better if both were capable of charging tablets and smartphones instead of just one mainly for tablets and the other mainly for smartphones. I would rate this a 5 out of 5 because it’s a great product and it has 2 usbs.

I've been using the Apple-supplied wall charger for my iPhone for years now. Long have I been frustrated by watching my phone like a hawk for it to reach 100%, then swapping the phone for wireless earbuds so I can go walk. I thought this was just a painful (albeit first-world) way of life, but now I see I was wrong - there is an answer, and it's New Trent's NT90C wall charger with two USB charging ports.The charger is small enough that it doesn't block the second plug on a standard wall outlet. The prongs on the charger fold in/out, so you can safely pack it in your backpack. It gives off a faint blue LED light when plugged in, not bright enough to disturb sleep if you have it plugged in your bedroom. The plastic case is rough enough that it's easy to pull out of the wall without gripping hard to a slippery smooth surface.I tested it with an iPhone 5, two iPad 3rd generation tablets, bluetooth earbuds and Zagg bluetooth iPad keyboard. The iPhone charged as fast as the Apple-supplied charger, whether it was the only device or combined with another device. The charger's two ports are labeled "Tablet/Smartphone" and "iPad/Smartphone", which is somewhat confusing. Charging an iPad and the iPhone together worked fine, regardless of which device was plugged into which USB port. I didn't measure the charging time on the iPad because, let's face it - watching an iPad charge is like watching paint dry. I did notice that the iPhone charged just as fast when the iPad was also plugged in. Charging two iPads at the same time did not work - only the port labeled "iPad/Smartphone" charged the iPad; the other iPad displayed the expected "Not Charging" error.The charger did get hot, but not disturbingly so. I've been using it for several days, and noticed it gets warm but not hot regardless of how many devices are plugged in.The New Trent NT90C dual USB wall charger was a great purchase - I like being able to charge both the iPad and the keyboard at the same time, or the iPhone and wireless earbuds at the same time. I'm happy enough that I plan on buying another unit, so I can charge the iPad and keyboard AND iPhone and earbuds all at the same time - what a crazy thought!
This is an awesome little device. Charges my iPad perfectly and would be interested in buying more. It is always out of stock because this little device is so good!

My high powered usb outlet has very fast charging capabilities. I have an HP touchpad that warns me all the time that the charger I was using is not the factory charger. That is probably because the chargers I’m using does not have enough power. Not with this charger! I started using it at my work desk because my usb ports on my computer could not charge my tablet. Now I have the duel port 2 amp outlets totaling 10 watts, my tablet charges fast and no warning on the screen that the charger was incompatible. The construction is high grade plastic with a sturdy flip plug which is great for traveling. I’m completely satisfied.
Fast charging and love the dual usb slot for charging 2 things at a time. The pins are set so as to minimize space usage on a plug
summary: Awesome charger for the house. Good placement of the pins.

text: The NT90C does its job --- reliable and relatively quick charging. Its size is not the smallest available though. It does not get overly warm, which is a plus.

The voltage is not so consistent and thus the Nexus 5 does not charge at full speed. Full speed with the original Nexus charger is at about 1050 mAh. This one provides 600-700 mAh and fluctuates a lot. That's not so good for the battery. Also the Apple port will only charge android phones at USB speed, which is about 100-200 mAh. The tests were done with several app for measuring current, such as CurrentWidget and GSam Battery Monitor
summary: Doesn't charge the Nexus 5 at high speed

text: This charger provides 2amps charging total which is good for all smartphones and tablets. Keep in mind though that since it is 2A, charging 2 tablets at once would charge a bit slow as most tablets use 2A alone. But with that aside, this is perfect for me since typically I only charge 1 device at a time, but I have both android and apple products, which have different charging cables. So with this charger, I can put one micro-usb cable for my Android devices, and one lightning cable for my iPhone 5S. I use another one of these with a lightning and 30-pin apple charger, for my iPad. I have a few of these placed throughout the house and have not had any problems with any of my devices including the Note 3, Note 2, S3, iPhone 5S, 4S, 3G, and iPad (3rd Gen). I replaced the single chargers around the house with this dual charger.It also has foldable prongs which is a plus when travelling. Construction wise, the charger feels solid.
summary: Convenient when you have multiple devices in the house.

text: This is an affordable and solidly built dual usb charger. I was seeking something that could be used to charge both my iPhone 4S (personal) and my iPhone 4S (work) at the same time. One of the annoyances I had was the fact that both chargers were taking up a spot on my power strip so I was seeking a device that could do both. When I found this number by New Trent, it was fantastic since it had great reviews, and when I got it, I had to admit that it was one of the best ones on the market at an affordable price. Would definitely recommend getting this if you have two devices to charge.One other neat thing to add is that the plug actually folds into the casing similar to the old style of iPad/iPod chargers. That's really nice for travel since you don't want to get the plug bent when thrown into your bag.

Well worth the price! This dual usb charger is perfect for charging any usb powered device. I tried charging my Ellipsis 7 tablet and my Droid Maxx smartphone at the same time. The both charged quickly with no issues at all. The plug is a little on the large side, but still fits easily into a standard electrical outlet.
This is one of the most popular gadgets in the house when we have guests. This helps maximize our charging regardless of electronic device.

The IMP90C is a great charger for all your mobile devices. The charger has a high-enough output to even satisfy the hungry tablet devices in your bag. It has a very solid feel to it, which means it will survive the beating it may take in your bag or on the road. The power prongs flip out, instead of some that slide out. It makes it very easy to plug into stiff outlets.
Works great. My wife and I charge our phones and tablets in the kitchen and not longer have to pull the light out of the other socket.
summary: Works great and not too expensive

text: Arrived on time and as promised.One port works intermittantly.After posting feedback, customer support contacted me immediately and offered to replace it. And no need for me to send the flakey one back. This is important because at this price point it doesn't make sense to pay for return shipping when you can just buy another one for the say $$$ as the return shipping. On a small ticket item like this, I'll just trash it, leave negative feedback and move on to another vendor.So, it's a welcome change when the vendor doesn't require the return.Cudo's to this vendor!Unfortunately, 1 star off for product arriving flakey .

The New Trent NT90C 10W 5V/2A Dual USB Ports high-speed AC Wall Charger for Smartphones, 5V Tablets and more is a neat USB charger. The dual USB charging ability is awesome, because it provides using less power adapters with your smartphones, tablets or iPads. I like that that the charger has folding prongs, which makes it easy to carry around with you. I was able to charge my iPhone and iPad at the same time without any issues. Great product!

The IMP90C is about the same size as the iPad charger, except I has two ports rather than one, which is really nice for travelling. It charges my devices just as fast as the stock iPad charger, except now I don't have to bring two chargers everywhere with me. The build quality seems pretty solid, overall a great device to have on hand.

Before I begin, this unit was provided to me at no charge by the manufacturer for evaluation. Past that point, it is up to me on how (and if) to review it.This one is pretty simple-- and, if you own a bunch of "newer generation" devices like the Amazon Kindles that don't come with a wall charger, you'll NEED something like this. text: I got this unit for charging my iPad Air, iPhone 5s, iPhone 4s, and iPad mini. It definitely helped us since most of our devices all plug in a wall plug that is in the kitchen near all the keys but there are only two wall sockets. It helps to tidy things up and get everything in order.I noted that you definitely have to be careful what plug you put things into though. I accidentally plugged my iPhone 5s in the phone slot but it wouldn't charge. That is because it requires the higher amps, which it has varying according to the USB slot that you use. It was easily solved but I definitely would have been bummed if I had just plugged it in without looking at the phone to notice it wasn't charging.The overall shape and ease of use were great. The blue LED light on top when plugged in was a good indicator that it was working.

text: There is really nothing bad anybody could say about this charger, it does what it is supposed to do and then some. text: To be honest, I feel like I can't pass up the opportunity to try out new chargers for my electronic devices--I feel like I never have enough of them around the house and I'm always transferring them from one room to another. I have Apple's wall chargers which work fine, but are expensive to replace (and don't work with my friend's DROID devices when they come over). I also have some generic ones that work, but are extremely slow. I wanted something that was fairly inexpensive, would work with multiple brands/devices and charged them fast.After reading some good reviews, I got the New Trent IMP90C dual USB wall charger to add to my collection, and it doesn't disappoint.As USB wall chargers go, it looks nice. It's fairly small, sleek and doesn't stick out like an eyesore. It has a little blue LED that lights up to let you know that you are plugged in and connected correctly.Performance-wise, the New Trent IMP90C shines. The benefits of having a dual charger instead of a single are pretty obvious. The IMP90C has dual 10W 5V/2.1 Amp USB chargers that had no problem charging my 3rd generation iPad and iPhone 4S simultaneously--and quickly. My iPhone charged from 3% to 100% charge in just over an hour and 10 minutes.I've been using the IMP90C for a few weeks now and can't find any reason not to give it a 5 star rating. The build quality is great and it works easily, quickly and couldn't be more convenient.Best home charger I have to date.
summary: Best and fastest home wall charger I've had to date!

text: When I received this USB charger from Amazon, I didn't expect much. In all honestly though i really love this. Also the prongs are really strong (unlike wall plugs with folding mechanisms where the weight of the block folds the prongs up and then the block falls out, users of the old AirPort Expresses would know what I mean.)Highly recommend as your next wall charger!

text: This charger is probably the best charger I have ever bought/experienced. It features two charging ports which allows for more devices to be charged at the same time, a LED light indicating its plugged in and charging, collapsible prongs and a compact design.I did a few tests on my various devices that i use every day. My reports show that my Samsung Galaxy s3 (i747) took only 3 hours to charge from 27% to 100% overnight. My regular Samsung charger that I got with my phone usually took about 5-6 hours or all night. I also charged my family's iPhone 4 and also a LG Xpression. Both these devices charging at the same time took about 4.7 hours, which is excellent.If you are always looking for a charger in your house from owning a lot of devices that need to be charged, then this is the product for you.Pros:Compact DesignFast Charging (I mean really fast)Dual Charging PortsCons:The only one I have is that the LED that shows if its plugged in is very dim and is hard to see if your not under low light. But it really doesn't bother me because my device tells me if its charging.Thanks to New Trent for sending this out to me.

I used this for my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 which has USB 3.0 charging. The fast USB 3.0 charging only works with 5V/2A outputs which this wall charger has thankfully! It's hard to find wall chargers with 2A outputs. This wall charger charges devices fast! It's a lifesaver whenever I need to charge my phone really quick. I'm a college student on the go a lot. I use this charger between lectures and have my phone charged 50% through a one hour lecture. If this wall charger is for your home, office, or portable emergency charger, it will not dissapoint. OH, DID I MENTION IT HAS TWO USB PORTS TO CHARGER TWO THINGS AT ONCE!? This is where it differentiate from other wall usb plugs. It saves space when you only have 2 outlets. You only use ONE outlet to charge two things at once which leaves the other outlet for other things (laptop chargers). This wall charger has a black matte plastic finish with a glossy end. The outlet prongs are retractable for easy storage.PROs:-Portable-Charge 2 things at once-Retractable prongs-Great build quality-Fast charging outputCONs:-It's a little larger than OEM and other wall chargers but keep in mind it charges TWO things at once lolOverall, this wall charger is awesome, it gets two thumbs up and my big toes up if that even means anything haha

The New Trent NT90C 10W 5V/27 Dual Port Charger is a great device. I am a true gadget geek and gave numerous devices that I charge with USB cables. It takes approximately twice the amount of time to charge my phone with this charger than the more popular PowerGen charger that I purchased after this one.

text: I've bought two of these recently, and both had the same quality-control issue with USB port alignment. The first charger had to be returned because it was simply impossible to plug anything in due to the USB ports being completely misaligned behind the port cutouts in the face plate. The second was also misaligned, but not nearly as much, so it's just barely possible to plug devices in, but only by inserting at an angle.Aside from the manufacturing defects, the charger works as advertised, and the AC prongs fold up for extreme portability. If not for the quality issues, it's a 5 out of 5, though do I prefer the 4-port over 2-port chargers.

I've been using the New Trent dual port charger for the last two days to recharge Kindle Fire HD 7" and Nexus 7 tablets, plus an iPhone 4 and a Samsung smartphone. At all times, I had two devices connected, and charging times seemed to be fairly close to the charging times with each device connected to its own dedicated charger. However, with the shared 2.1 amps of output current from the charger, some combinations of devices would recharge more slowly than normal. The tradeoff is the ability to recharge two devices simultaneously from a single charger.The charger appears to be very well made, and it's compact enough to stow away in a backpack or laptop case for traveling. The prongs in the plug fold into the charger, so they don't punch through the sides of the backpack or case.There's nothing glamorous about an AC charger, but they're a necessity today for most people, and the New Trent dual port charger is a solid performer that I can recommend without reservation.A product sample was provided by the manufacturer for review purposes.

UPDATE 2-13: I had to replace the charger when the usb of the lesser power quit working, the 2A port was just fine. On the 2nd one, they both worked great for a month and then the same thing happened, weaker port just quit working. 2A port is just fine. Not sure why this happened, but disconcerting that it happened on both chargers. So I lower my rating to TWO STARTSI really like this charger. I like that the prongs fold down for traveling, it's fairly small and only takes up one outlet. I am able to reduce a charger port off my multi-outlet and then love this for when I am traveling. It's lighter weight than I expected, but as long as it holds up that doesn't bother me. With devices charging rapidly, I can switch out the family's phones when we are at a hotel and not have to worry about kids forgetting their charger after we leave or fighting over outlets.
summary: perfect for my needs... or so I thought

text: Having been sorely let down by some experiences with docks for my iPhone 4 and iPad 3, I've gone back to wall chargers. This one is the best! It's easy to switch out cables for Android and Apple devices, and in four months, it's never failed. If you accidentally plug into the wrong port, the device clearly tells you.The charger itself is sturdy and solid. There's a definite difference between the New Trent and a couple of other off-brand chargers I have, and this is the one I take on trips.Very pleased.

This is a wall charger that has two usb ports for charging different devices. Both ports output 2.1A which is enough to charge 2 tablets at the same time.I like the size of this charger. It is rather small and doesn’t block any of the other ports on my power strip. Also, I like the fact the LED on it is NOT annoyingly bright, it’s actually pretty dim which is good so it won’t keep me up if it’s by my bed. (I usually just put a piece of electrical tape on light like that if they are too bright anyway.)Other than that this devices does what it says. I’ve used it to charge my phone and my iPad at the same time. I’ve also used it to charge my iPad and my wife’s at the same time too just to make sure it could and it worked just fine.

This product is simple but that doesn't detract it from being great. It is a simple two port charger that works perfectly and is well built.The best aspect of this charger is that one of the ports is a higher amperage charger that tablets require. Before getting this charger, I had two USB chargers on desk, one for my phone (Galaxy S3) and one for my tablet (Nexus 7). Now, with this charger, I only have the single charger, leaving additional outlets open on my desk for charging. This is even more advantageous for traveling, where I no longer have to bring two chargers and I no longer have to be sure that I have a charger capable of charging a tablet. It sounds simple, but packing a single charger is so much easier.The build quality of the charger is also very high. The flip out two prong port is simple and makes storage much easier. It feels sturdy and I'm sure it will last for quite a while.My one small gripe of the charger is that the two ports, while being useful for charging a tablet (high amperage) and a phone (low amperage) simultaneously, they are poorly labeled and I wasn't certain which port was which. Quickly looking at other reviews reveals that the top port is the high amperage port, and the bottom is low amperage, which I have confirmed.Last but not least, something that many people may not notice, but is a huge plus for me, is the small dim LED that is on the charger. While having an LED is useful for ensuring it's operating properly, the LED on my old charger was bright enough to be a nightlight. This new charger LED is perfect: it's bright enough to see clearly, but is barely visible at night.Overall, I will be recommending this charger to friends. It's well built and works exactly as described.

text: This is a great wall charger, and I'd have given it 5 stars if I didn't have to ask hubby (the electrical go-to person in the family) to explain why, if it says it's a 10W 5V/2A Dual USB charger, one port says Tablet/Smartphone and the other says iPad/Smartphone, and some reviews say the ports aren't equal, and do I have to worry about plugging something in where I shouldn't. All I remember is, it has something to do with the 10W and I don't need to worry. I can plug whatever we have into either port and it won't do any damage, and it will charge our devices just fine, maybe some a little faster than others. So with that knowledge, and the fact that I read it has short circuit and overcharge protection, I do just that.For the most part, I use it to plug our PowerPaks in at the end of the day. We both have an iPhone 4S and we both tend to need power boosts before the end of the day. text: I decided to purchase this New Trent, 10W 5V/2A Dual Port high-speed USB AC wall charger (NT90C/IMP90C) over two months ago and so far it held up well.What's included in the box?* New Trent USB AC Wall Charger (NT90C/IMP90C)!After searching through a dozen chargers, I decided to go with New Trent due to the name brand familiarity and the average reviews for this simple device. It should be no brainer. Connect the device to the wall and charge either at 5V2A or at 5V1A. For those who aren't technically inclined, you'll want to make sure your USB AC Wall Charge have at least a 5V2A USB port available for either faster charging speeds or high wattage demands for certain tablets to charge. 5V1A port can charge any smartphone, but for tablets it'll just power it but not charge it from my experience.That information in hand, the first thing you need to know about this USB AC Wall charger is that it has two outputs. The top output is 5V/1A (can charge anything except tablets with 10W demands). The bottom output is 5V/2A (Charge tablets with 10W demands and anything else a bit faster). When I refer to the top and bottom ports, this is with wording right-side up, so you can read them properly. The charger basically splits the 10 Watts delivered from the outlet. So in a nutshell, expect reduced charging speeds with two devices connected to the charger.As for which device it can charge...as long as your device can be charged with a USB cable and doesn't require a separate power adapter, it'll work. The Samsung Galaxy tablets may require a separate USB adapter to get it charging. I do agree with many other reviewers, they should have been more clearer about which ports has which amperage. But since the unit is compact and doesn't cover 2 outlets, it's a keeper. This unit works as advertise. I'll post any future comments if this device malfunctions or breaks down.

Used this product with a Google Nexus 7, Droid Razr, PowerLine Mobile AC Outlet - DC to AC Converter, IPod Touch and theNew Trent: NT120C CarbonPak - (12000mAh) Portable Back Up External Battery Charger/Power Bank/Power Pack for Apple: iPad 4 / 3 / 2/ iPad mini, iPhone 5 / 4S / 4 /3GS, iPod Touch (all version); Samsung: Galaxy Note, S4 / S3 / S2, Galaxy Nexus ; Google: N...Overall, the IMP90C does exactly what it is supposed to do....rapidly charge phones and tablets. It fully charged my Nexus 7 in about 2.5 hours and my Droid in just a little over 2 hours. It even (very slowly) charges other devices not described in the description details. Even though it slowly charges the "other" devices not listed, it is still better than it not being able to charge them at all.PROS: Small & compact making it easy to take along with you.Hide away/fold out prongsRapidly charges phones and tables as specified (even during HD graphic RPGameplay)Charges gadgets that aren't not described in the description details.Solid build of device and prongs.CONS: Hard to keep the IMP90C in the wall when some sockets are upside down.Easy to forget which USB port to plug which device in. Ports need to be labeledOVERALL RATING: 5 Stars - The device does exactly as described. It evencharges "other" devices not included in the description.

text: The New Trent 10W (5.1V/2.1A) USB Dual Port Power Adapter (NT90C) is a great replacement for wall chargers that come included with cell phones, tablets, Bluetooth headphones, external batteries and other small electronics. In many cases these products don't even come with wall chargers. But the ones that do, these wall chargers don't even come close in quality or usefulness to The New Trent (NT90C).1. NT90C has dual port so you can charge two devices at the same time.2. Charging time is faster than regular wall charger. I tested charging times with all electronic gadgets I have: iPhone 5S, iPad Mini, Samsung Galaxy Tab, BlackBerry PlayBook, various Bluetooth headphones, New Trent external batteries.3. Well built for traveling. Light but sturdy construction with collapsible prongs. Does not feel cheap when you hold it. And if you have two devices, you can carry only one wall charger.The important fact that should be known about New Trent (NT90C) is that two USB ports are not the same. And not the same in regards only to iPad. Both USB ports marked as such. Top USB port marked "Tablet/Smartphone" and the bottom USB port marked "iPad/Smartphone". Not sure why it's done that way, since top USB port can charge any device except iPad and bottom USB port can charge any device including iPad. My only problem with this is one has to remember which USB port charges iPad because markings are not lighted or highly visible. So you might be in a hurry, stick iPad into top USB port only to find out two hours later that your iPad did not get charged. IPad does display message "not charging" when plugged to top USB port but you have to wait and see that message appear.For this I would rate this product 4 1/2 stars Instead of 5 stars.
