text: With so many mobile devices in a household, it's sometimes tough to plug multiple ones in at the same time in the same place. This wall charger from New Trent allows two USB devices to be plugged into the same outlet.DesignIt's compact enough to allow multiple ones to be plugged into the same electrical receptacle. In addition, it can be carried around easily as the prongs fold up.AccessoryThere are no accessories included.ChargingIt is rated at 2.1A combined, which means that charging two smartphones simultaneously should be no problem. However, if you plug in devices that need more than a combined 2.1A, it will take longer to charge both devices. I tried charging a New Trent external battery and my smartphone and found that the smartphone was slower to charge than normal.UPDATE (10/30/2013)After using this charger for a short while, I found an issue with it. I noticed that if I would plug my smartphone (Motorola Photon 4G) into the top USB port, my phone would not show that it was getting charged. I am only able to charge it in the bottom USB port. However, my wife is able to plug her smartphone (HTC Evo 3D) into either USB port without any issues. My guess is that the top port doesn't provide as much amperage as the bottom one, and my phone requires more amperage than my wife's phone. It's not a big issue for us as I simply always plug my phone into the bottom, but this could be an issue if you're trying to plug in two devices that have higher power requirements. I contacted New Trent about this issue, and they think it's related to circuity in the charger for iPads that is causing this issue, but they are looking into it. They were not able to give me any specifics on the amperage for each of the USB ports.UPDATE (10/31/2013)I heard back from New Trent. They said that the charger can output 2.1A max combined, but that the bottom USB port can supply up to 2.1A (if only one device is connected), while the top USB port can output up to 1A.Pros: Compact, easy-to-use, allows two devices to be charged using one outlet.Cons: Charging multiple devices may take longer to charge or may not charge the device in the top USB port (see updates)

PRO's:--Price is right.--Having the option of connecting two devices simultaneously is nice.--Compact size.CON's:--The ports aren't actually labeled to indicate which is the higher-amp one (to use with an iPad vs. an iPhone, for example).--Not grounded (although, really, most inexpensive AC adapters for USB-connected devices aren't grounded, either).BOTTOM LINE:Inexpensive, flexible for multiple (and different kinds of) devices, easily used for travel. Just wish the ports were labeled to differentiate the lower and higher power of each.

text: I am a recent convert to the iPad and iPad mini. I was looking for accessories and came across New Trent on Amazon. I purchased the Airbender Mini NT31B case/keyboard. Awesome product, made me more efficient in my job. I liked the keyboard and decided to purchase additional items from New Tent based upon the quality of the case/keyboard. I ordered the Dual port charger, NT90C to save space in my backpack. It arrived quickly and I tried it out as soon as I opened the package to charge my phone (Motorola Droid Razor Maxx and iPad Mini. With the two seperate ports the charger worked out great. Charged quickly and one less item to carry around in the backpack.

Priced just right, the NT90C provides the power and the dual ports that make this a truly functional charger. With the proliferation of USB-powered devices and battery packs, you can never have enough chargers around the home, at work, and in the car. I currently use this in the garage and its simple and hardy design works to a tee. I have charged iOS devices, tablets, battery packs, and my Sony camera, all very swiftly. The only improvements I would suggest include: better labeling of individual port powers, and some indicator of usage (like LEDs). Overall though, excellent value and great to have several of these scattered throughout your home and office!

The charger works exactly as it's supposed to; it charges anything that I want, and the dual ports allow me to charge multiple devices, which is great. It's small, and the folding prongs make it easy to carry around in a bag without worrying about the prongs getting damaged or putting holes in your bag. There are a few things that could be improved though. The blue indicator light is unnecessary, because most phones, tablets, or whatever else you're charging with the charger have their own indicator lights. This makes the blue indicator light on the charger redundant. The labels for the ports are also not very useful. The top port is labeled "Tablet/Smartphone" and the bottom is labeled "iPad/Smartphone." These labels aren't useful because the an iPad is a tablet, and the word smartphone is used for both ports. It would be better if the ports were labeled with the output in amperes or some other way that's not as confusing. Still a great product, but small changes could make it better.
summary: New Trent Dual USB Wall Charge 2.1A Max Output (NT90C):

text: I own quite a few New Trent products, and this charger is a very handy- and necessary item if you have any of the New Trent battery packs like the Powerpak Ultra or the Powerpak Xtreme, as those products only come with a USB charging cord. This NT90C charger will provide quicker charge times and obviously allow you to charge two devices at once. The metal prongs fold inward to allow for easy carry or storage options. It will charge device at 2.1 amps or two devices at 1 amps each. Well though out design and has a high quality feel to it. Definitely worth the price, even better as an Amazon Prime member!

Ok. I have gone through a handful of these types of chargers, and none of them seem to last. This one only lasted a couple months. text: I love the size and convenience of it. I took it with me on a six hour road trip last weekend. We have an electric outlet in our hybrid, so I was able to plug in directly. I charged my NT120T and cell phone during the trip by using the IMP90C. It freed up the cigarette lighter for my wife's charger and the one in the back for my daughter's.This is such a nice little device. I didn't know exactly how I would use it at first, but it quickly became apparent that I could use it in a lot of situations. I mostly use it now to keep my two New Trent battery chargers charged. It is perfect for that since I can just set them down right next to each other and not have to worry about trailing cables all over the house.

The labeling of the ports could be a little more obvious, but the bottom port is capable of a full 2.1A output. The top (middle) one is limited to 1A, so make sure to plug in your power hungry devices to the one closest to the edge.Overall this worked flawlessly and it is great to have the dual ports for multi-device charging. Another excellent feature is that the plug folds into the device which makes it MUCH easier for transport while traveling and not resulting in the tines getting bent or poking other things. There is a blue LED on the top of the charger as well that provides an indicator of power which is a nice touch.It would be nice if either port would do the high capacity charging, or if the device supported the 2.1A on both ports simultaneously as devices are moving more and more towards this power hungry nature. In the end though, this is an excellent charger with only minor gripes that are relatively inconsequential.Highly recommend the product.

It took some experimenting to figure out which port was the tablet (high-amp) port, and which was the phone (low-amp) port.I measured the charging rate on a phone, and got 1742A (I think that is the max it can charge at). On my Android tablet, I measured 1929mA.For either device, this is a lot better than the 1.5 I was getting with the best charger I had before this, and SCADS better than the chargers that came with them... lots cheaper, too.Next, I think I'll take a look at their car charger and see how it performs....

text: There will be many times when you are away from your computer and wish to charge your cellphone or other electronic device such as your external battery. ❗ - I wanted to start things off by giving tips to applying a screen protector properly: - ❗1) If you want to put one of these on, the best time is IMMEDIATELY after buying a new phone. Don't let the salesman/woman take off the plastic covering and skip to STEP 52) If you have already used your phone and now decided that you need a screen protector (as most people are in this boat) gather these supplies:-Lens Cleaner (or anything else with a high alcohol content) [simply chemistry, alcohol evaporates quickly]-Lint free cloth (such as silk) [included in this purchase]-Credit Card3) Pour a small amount of your lens cleaner onto your lint free cloth and liberally clean all surfaces of the phone4) Repeat a few times to make sure all debris is removed from the screen5) Lift the bottom of the film from the backside (side that will be touching your phone) DO NOT TAKE OFF THE WHOLE FILM YET6) Place the bottom part of the cover on your phone and align it on the edges of your phone7) Use a credit card to smooth out any and all bubbles that may be present8) SLOWLY go back and fourth from using your credit card and removing a SMALL amount of the thin film from the back of the screen protector9) !THIS IS THE STEP MOST PEOPLE MISS!After your installation process is complete, try your best to wait about 30 minutes to an hour to really let to adhesive set. This will prevent any debris from gathering under your screen.If you followed all of those steps, you shouldn't have any problems getting a bubble-free screen protector!✅ - What really sets this brand apart from the others is that they don't have that sort of sticky feeling that most screen protectors are plagued with. You know what I'm talking about if you've used your friends phone and you have a hard time sliding your finger across the screen. This screen protector does not have that problem at all!✅ - Another great feature about this product is that it prevents fingerprints. Most phones come with the coveted olio-phobic coatings that are great for about a day.✅ - Also, one thing I have noticed with a lot of screen protectors is that after a few weeks, the edges start to peel off. The screen protector my mom has on her phone (something she bought at verizon) gets fingerprints like crazy and puts a nasty hazy glare on her screen and after about 3 weeks, about a third of the protector started to peel away. That alone is proof to me that the quality of a screen protector DOES matter.I can't recmmend it highly enough!✅ - I give this product my highest recommendation especially when following my suggested steps to putting this on

The main vulnerability is when dropped the screens have a tendency to crack and craze on impact. Simple screen "protectors" such as this one do NOT protect from such hazards.Lastly I must live in a very dusty environment, I have YET to succeed at putting on a protector on with no apparent bubbles caused by tiny bits of dust.
